Luke 13:34—Jesus depicts his desire to gather Jerusalem as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The edge, corner, or hem of a garment, symbolizing covenantal covering, marital protection, or claimed responsibility.","basis":["Ruth 3:9—Ruth asks Boaz to spread his kanaph over her, commonly understood as a request for marriage and protection.","Ezekiel 16:8—God spreads the corner of his garment over Jerusalem in a covenant or marriage image.","1 Samuel 24:4–5, 11—the kanaph of Saul’s robe is cut, sometimes interpreted in relation to royal authority, though the immediate sense is the garment’s corner."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The specially fringed corner of an Israelite garment, representing covenant identity, obedience, and holiness.","basis":["Numbers 15:38–40—Tassels are placed on the kanaph of garments as reminders of God’s commandments.","Deuteronomy 22:12—Tassels are prescribed for the corners of the garment.","Matthew 9:20–22; 37:9—Cherubim overshadow the mercy seat with their wings.","1 Kings 6:24–27; 8:6–7—Cherubic wings overshadow the ark in the temple.","Isaiah 6:2—Seraphim use their wings in the vision of God’s holiness.","Ezekiel 1:6–11, 23–24;
